elements.text: [Bug 19135] New: Bug with CHARSXP lifetime assumption by ALTSTRING elt method

Bug ID: 19135
           Summary: Bug with CHARSXP lifetime assumption by ALTSTRING elt
                    method
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: All
                OS: All
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee:

Here is a bug report where R functions mistakenly assumes the lifetime of
ALTREP elements from package classes.

Although this requires package interaction, I believe the bug is more on the R
side, because there is no specification on requirements for CHARSXP lifetime
from ALTREP classes. The only relevant discussion I found is in 2021:

# R CMD SHLIB mre.c
  dyn.load("mre.so")
  target <- rawToChar(as.raw(c(

(0x61L, 64L), 0xe9L)))
  Encoding(target) <- "latin1"

  x <- .Call("mre_make", 64*1024*1024, 0)
  charmatch(x, target)
   *** caught segfault ***
  address 0x7a5419901040, cause 'memory not mapped'



In
(src/main/unique.c), the input is ASCII, so the first element

returns a pointer to the CHARSXP
directly. However, because it is ALTREP, that CHARSXP is not anchored in a
vector. Then the 2nd argument needs UTF8 translation because it is latin1,
which causes an allocation and garbage collection of the container of

.

Here is another example using substr:

  # R CMD SHLIB mre.c
  dyn.load("mre.so")

  x <- .Call("mre_make", 64*1024*1024, 0)   # 0: Elt does not retain the
CHARSXP
  substr(x, 1L, 10L)
  # *** caught segfault ***
  # address 0x7c9e13fff042, cause 'memory not mapped'



Suggested fixes:

Improve ALTREP documentation to require stable lifetime from ALTREP string
classes. Document what is expected of ALTREP classes. It is unclear whether
ALTREP classes are required to keep CHARSXPs alive. If that is intended, I
believe it should be documented.

Alternatively: update these functions (and others) to not assume CHARSXP
lifetime is stable.

*[Bug 19136] New: person() role-matching doesn't work*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19136>

            Bug ID: 19136
           Summary: person() role-matching doesn't work
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Misc
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

`.canonicalize_person_role()` (`citation.R:194`) validates `person()` roles
against the MARC relator codes and, per its own comment, intends to be nice
about it:

```
    ## Be nice.  Given roles must either exactly match the role code,
    ## or be uniquely pmatchable modulo case against the role terms.
    pos <- which(<http://is.na|is.na>(match(role, MARC_relator_db$code)))
    if(length(pos)) {
        ind <- pmatch(tolower(role[pos]),
                      tolower(MARC_relator_db$name),   # <- no such column
                      0L)
```

However, this fails as the `MARC_relator_db` has no column called 'name'; I
suspect the matching here should be against 'term'. Quick patch:

```
Index: src/library/utils/R/citation.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/utils/R/citation.R      (revision 90394)
+++ src/library/utils/R/citation.R      (working copy)
@@ -199,7 +199,7 @@
     pos <- which(<http://is.na|is.na>(match(role, MARC_relator_db$code)))
     if(length(pos)) {
         ind <- pmatch(tolower(role[pos]),
-                      tolower(MARC_relator_db$name),
+                      tolower(MARC_relator_db$term),
                       0L)
         role[pos[ind > 0L]] <- MARC_relator_db$code[ind]
         if(any(ind <- (ind == 0L))) {
```

Or, alternatively, if the intention is to preserve the current behavior, that
block of code could be removed.

(Strictly speaking, from what I can see, R-exts doesn't document the use of the
full term variants here either.)

*[Bug 19137] New: LINE_DIRECTIVE nodes get parent=0 in getParseData*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19137>

            Bug ID: 19137
           Summary: LINE_DIRECTIVE nodes get parent=0 in getParseData
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: All
                OS: All
            Status: NEW
          Severity: minor
          Priority: P5
         Component: Language
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:michaelchirico4@gmail.com|michaelchirico4@gmail.com>

```
s = '
{
#line 1 "file.R"
  x <- 1
}
'
cat(s, file=tmp<-tempfile())
getParseData(parse(tmp))
```

has structure:

```
   line1 col1 line2 col2 id parent          token terminal             text
18     2    1     5    1 18      0           expr    FALSE                 
3      2    1     2    1  3     18            '{'     TRUE                {
5      3    1     3   16  5      0 LINE_DIRECTIVE     TRUE #line 1 "file.R"
13     4    3     4    8 13     18           expr    FALSE                 
7      4    3     4    3  7      9         SYMBOL     TRUE                x
9      4    3     4    3  9     13           expr    FALSE                 
8      4    5     4    6  8     13    LEFT_ASSIGN     TRUE               <-
10     4    8     4    8 10     11      NUM_CONST     TRUE                1
11     4    8     4    8 11     13           expr    FALSE                 
16     5    1     5    1 16     18            '}'     TRUE                }
```

IINM, it makes most sense for `LINE_DIRECTIVE` to get the same `parent` as
would a `COMMENT`. I'm not the most familiar with this feature of the language,
but having `parent=0` does strike me as incorrect for a directive inside an `{`
expression.

This came about from {lintr} making the (IMHO correct) assumption that such
`parent==0` for a non-top-level expression is impossible:

```
lintr::lint(tmp)
# Error in expression_xmls[[i]] : subscript out of bounds
```

Which I encountered in the R test suite:

<https://svn.r-project.org/browse/R/trunk/tests/reg-tests-2.R?op=blame&rev=88200#l3394>

(PS my first time trying the /browse/ view to share a source link, is this the
easiest way to share a perma-link? Computing the 'blame' page took several
minutes. The GitHub mirror can generate such perma-links ~instantly:
<https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/084423720a65e00a4bec911e66cffd2881f925ac/tests/reg-tests-2.R#L3391-L3396)>

*[Bug 19127] Sys.timezone() gives strange warning in non-UTF-8 encoding*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19127>

--- Comment #2 from Michael Chirico (<mailto:michaelchirico4@gmail.com|michaelchirico4@gmail.com>) ---
For future reference: this originated from a patched version of `systemd 260`.

Gemini offers the following diagnosis (unverified, looks plausible, run
alongside local clone of systemd):

---

### Verification on systemd 255 vs Ubuntu 24.04 & openSUSE

The issue **is present in systemd 255 as well**; it did not break between 255
and 261. The difference observed between Ubuntu 24.04 and openSUSE Tumbleweed
is caused by distribution locale packaging and the specific day of the week
tested:

1. **Ubuntu 24.04 (`locales` package)**:
   - Ubuntu and Debian do not compile legacy 8-bit locales by default. Unless
`lv_LV ISO-8859-13` is manually added to `/etc/locale.gen` and compiled via
`locale-gen` (or `localedef`), `lv_LV` does not exist on the system (only
`lv_LV.UTF-8` exists if Latvian was installed).
   - When running `LC_TIME=lv_LV timedatectl status` without the locale
installed, `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` in `timedatectl.c:1019` fails to load
`lv_LV` and silently falls back to `C` / `C.UTF-8`. In `C` locale, `strftime`
emits ASCII weekday names (`Wed ...`), which are valid UTF-8, so `timedatectl`
succeeded.
   - If `lv_LV` (ISO-8859-13) is compiled on Ubuntu 24.04 using `localedef -i
lv_LV -f ISO-8859-13 lv_LV`, **systemd 255 fails with the exact same error**:

     Failed to print table: Invalid argument

2. **openSUSE Tumbleweed (`glibc-locale-base`)**:
   - openSUSE packages pre-compiled legacy glibc locales out of the box.
`LC_TIME=lv_LV` successfully activates `lv_LV.ISO-8859-13` (Latin-7).

3. **Weekday dependency (`strftime("%a")`)**:
   - In `lv_LV.ISO-8859-13`, the Latvian abbreviated weekday names defined in
glibc locale data include non-breaking spaces (byte `0xA0` in Latin-7 /
ISO-8859-13):
     - Monday: `P\xa0`
     - Tuesday: `O\xa0`
     - Wednesday: `T\xa0`
     - Thursday: `C\xa0`
     - Friday: `Pk` *(pure ASCII)*
     - Saturday: `S\xa0`
     - Sunday: `Sv` *(pure ASCII)*
   - On **Friday** and **Sunday**, `strftime("%a")` produces pure ASCII, so
`timedatectl status` will actually succeed even in `lv_LV.ISO-8859-13`. On the
other 5 weekdays, byte `0xA0` triggers the UTF-8 parser failure.

---

### 2. Culprit Commits and Root Cause

The failure occurs through the following call chain:

1. `print_status_info()` (timedatectl.c#L101-L108) calls `strftime(a, sizeof a,
"%a %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z", &tm)` and passes the string into the table formatter
via `table_add_many()`.
2. `table_print_full()` (format-table.c#L2316) calls
`table_data_requested_width_height()` (format-table.c#L2004) ->
`console_width_height()` (format-table.c#L1958).
3. `console_width_height()` (format-table.c#L1984-L1988) calls
`utf8_console_width()` (src/basic/utf8.c#L601) to compute character cell
widths.
4. `utf8_char_console_width()` (src/basic/utf8.c#L178) calls
`utf8_encoded_to_unichar()` (src/basic/utf8.c#L61). When it encounters byte
`0xA0` without a UTF-8 multi-byte prefix, it returns `-EINVAL`.
5. `utf8_console_width()` (src/basic/utf8.c#L616) returns `SIZE_MAX`.
6. `console_width_height()` (src/shared/format-table.c#L1988) catches `k ==
SIZE_MAX` and returns `-EINVAL`.
7. `table_print_or_warn()` (src/shared/format-table.c#L2678) catches `-EINVAL`
and logs `Failed to print table: %m` (`Invalid argument`).

#### Working As Intended (WAI):

systemd strictly assumes UTF-8 across all internal tools, logs, configuration
files, IPC interfaces, and terminal output formatting. Non-UTF-8 locales are
explicitly considered legacy/obsolete upstream:
* Commit `a7d9fccd0e` (*"locale-util: suppress non-UTF-8 locales when
enumerating them"*, v243) explicitly filters out legacy non-UTF-8 locales by
default (*"Filter out non-UTF-8 locales, because it's 2019, by default"*).
